heading: Client classes that call the server
body: Use HTTPClient on a client class whose methods have empty bodies: a client is a contract with no implementation, and Tachyon writes each request. Lua has no tab here, because the build refuses HTTPClient in Lua Tac code with TY1308. C++ has no tab here either, because a C++ client has no Setup adapter yet: it always sends its requests through the browser (see the C++ section of Calling the server; ADR 0099). Use GetRequest, PostRequest, PutRequest, PatchRequest or DeleteRequest on its methods. Needs injects the client into a service without a constructor. Browser JavaScript and TypeScript clients send bounded JSON to the same origin. They reject redirects, send no credentials and cancel when their owner is disposed. Other languages declare the client as a contract (an interface, trait, protocol or abstract interface class), and its Setup may give it an explicitly configured HTTP adapter. Tachyon builds the client and its context from the Setup that the `setup` option names; without the option it uses `<Name>Setup`, such as `CatalogSetup` for `CatalogClient`. In Dart, Rust, Go, Kotlin, Swift, Java, Ruby, C# and F#, a client whose Setup gives it no adapter sends its request through the browser to the server of the page, without cookies (see the sections below). A Dart, Rust, Go, Kotlin, Swift, Java, Ruby or C# service can inject the client with Needs too. In Ruby, `#[Needs]` stands above `attr_reader :catalog_client`, with `# @return [CatalogClient]` between them. A service in the other languages builds the client itself. In this example, CatalogSetup's adapter answers with two product names. Like a Spring @Configuration, a Setup is configured once per page: every client, store and service context built from it shares the same adapters until the last of them is disposed. In Yon it is configured once per server process. For now, the browser services in Swift, Kotlin, Java, C#, F#, Rust and Dart each still get their own copy of a Setup, so two of these services that use the same client do not share its adapters yet. The Go services of a page build into one Go package with one Setup, so they share it (ADR 0045). JavaScript and TypeScript services import one Setup class from the shared behavior runtime module, so they share its definition, its static fields and its adapters (ADR 0022). The clients inside one service already share them. A Service cannot also be an HTTPClient (TY1308). A Tac service never calls fetch itself (TY1361). A read is sent no-store by default, so it is always fresh. To keep a read, use the cache annotations on the client: CacheSettings on the class, Cached on the read, and ClearCache or UpdateCache on the write that changes it. In JavaScript and TypeScript a Cached GET is also a public read, so the service worker may answer it by the manifest's tac.cache rules. HTTPClient takes no cache option: the build refuses `{"cache": ...}` and names CacheSettings and Cached (ADR 0087). See the [routing annotation glossary](/docs/routing-annotations). Another host needs its name in `tac.outgoing.hosts` or `outgoing.hosts`; Tachyon refuses every other host when it builds and when it runs (`TY1326`).
